experiences.name: Maasai Mara Great Migration Safari
experiences.description: Witness the world-famous Great Migration where millions of wildebeest, zebras, and gazelles cross the Mara River in a dramatic spectacle. Game drives in open 4x4 vehicles offer close encounters with the Big Five including lions, elephants, leopards, buffaloes, and rhinos in their natural habitat.
experiences.location: Maasai Mara National Reserve, Narok County

experiences.name: Amboseli Elephant Watching with Kilimanjaro Backdrop
experiences.description: Observe the largest free-roaming elephant herds in Africa against the stunning backdrop of Mount Kilimanjaro. Amboseli is renowned for its large elephant population and offers exceptional photography opportunities with dramatic landscapes including swamps, savannah, and volcanic ash plains.

experiences.name: Ol Pejeta Conservancy Rhino Tracking
experiences.description: Track both black and white rhinos on foot with expert rangers at Ol Pejeta, home to the last two northern white rhinos on Earth. The conservancy also shelters chimpanzees, lions, and wild dogs. A guided bush walk brings you intimately close to nature in a way traditional game drives cannot.

experiences.name: Lake Nakuru Flamingo & Bird Safari
experiences.description: Explore Lake Nakuru National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site famous for its millions of pink flamingos that paint the lake's shores in vivid color. The park also hosts Rothschild giraffes, white rhinos, and over 450 bird species, making it a paradise for nature lovers and birdwatchers.
experiences.location: Lake Nakuru National Park, Nakuru County

experiences.name: Maasai Cultural Village & Bush Dinner Under the Stars
experiences.description: Immerse yourself in authentic Maasai culture with a guided village visit, traditional dances, and storytelling around a campfire. Cap the evening with a bush dinner under a canopy of stars in the open savannah, enjoying locally inspired cuisine including nyama choma (roasted meat) and ugali while listening to the sounds of the African wilderness.
experiences.location: Maasai Mara Conservancy Villages, Narok County

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Kenya
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Maasai Mara National Reserve, Narok County Boutique Stay
hotel.location: Maasai Mara National Reserve, Narok County

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00. Rest and prepare for transfer.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Nairobi's Jomo Kenyatta International Airport at 13:00. Clear customs and immigration, collect luggage, and arrange a budget shared shuttle or matatu (local bus) transfer toward Narok County (approx. 5–6 hours). Grab a quick bite at the airport or a roadside stop en route.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at your boutique stay in Maasai Mara National Reserve, Narok County. Check in, freshen up, and settle into your accommodation. Take a short walk around the lodge grounds as the sun sets over the savanna. Enjoy a welcome dinner at the lodge.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable — in transit
meals.lunch: Roadside nyama choma (grilled meat) or chapati with beans at a local duka (small shop) along the Narok highway — budget KES 200–400
meals.dinner: Lodge communal dinner or self-catered ugali with sukuma wiki (collard greens) and beans at the boutique stay — budget KES 500–800

day_by_day.notes: Book your shared shuttle or matatu in advance from Nairobi CBD (e.g., from Narok Bus Stage). Carry enough Kenyan shillings as ATMs are scarce near the Mara. Dress in layers — evenings in the Mara can be cool despite warm daytime temperatures.

day_by_day.morning: Rise before dawn for an early morning game drive inside Maasai Mara National Reserve. July is peak Great Migration season — witness massive herds of wildebeest and zebra crossing the plains. Look out for the Big Five: lion, leopard, elephant, buffalo, and rhino. Bring binoculars and a camera.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the lodge for a late brunch. Rest during the hottest part of the day (early afternoon). In the mid-afternoon, take a guided nature walk on the lodge perimeter with a Maasai guide to learn about local flora, medicinal plants, and animal tracks — a low-cost or free activity often offered by budget lodges.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a sundowner on the lodge grounds watching the spectacular African sunset over the savanna. Gather around a campfire with fellow travelers and exchange stories. Dinner at the lodge.

meals.breakfast: Early packed breakfast or flask of chai (tea) provided by the lodge before the game drive — included or KES 200–300
meals.lunch: Late brunch at the lodge: fried eggs, toast, fruit, and chai — budget KES 300–500
meals.dinner: Lodge dinner: lentil stew, rice, chapati, and seasonal vegetables — budget KES 500–700

day_by_day.notes: Arrange your game drive through the lodge or a local budget operator — shared game drives in a 4WD vehicle cost approximately KES 3,000–5,000 per person including park fees (park entry is approx. KES 2,000–3,500 for non-residents). Always follow ranger guidelines and never feed wildlife.

day_by_day.morning: Second early morning game drive focusing on the Mara River crossing points — July is prime time to witness the dramatic wildebeest river crossings, one of nature's greatest spectacles. Position near the river banks with your guide and wait patiently for the herds to cross, battling Nile crocodiles and strong currents.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local Maasai village (manyatta) near the reserve boundary. Participate in a cultural exchange — learn about Maasai traditions, beadwork, and daily life. Purchase handmade souvenirs directly from artisans to support the community. Negotiate respectfully and budget KES 500–1,500 for a village visit fee.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the lodge before dusk. Spend the evening star-gazing from the lodge grounds — the Mara's dark skies offer stunning visibility of the Milky Way. Attend an optional campfire storytelling session led by Maasai guides.

meals.breakfast: Pre-dawn packed snack: boiled eggs, mandazi (fried dough), and thermos of chai — KES 150–250
meals.lunch: Simple picnic lunch in the bush (arranged with the lodge): sandwiches, fruit, and juice — KES 300–400
meals.dinner: Communal lodge dinner: grilled chicken, ugali, kachumbari (tomato-onion salad), and soup — KES 500–800

day_by_day.notes: The Maasai village visit fee usually includes a guided tour and a cultural dance performance. Confirm costs upfront to avoid surprises. Wear neutral-colored clothing (khaki, olive, beige) for game drives — bright colors can disturb wildlife. Apply sunscreen and carry insect repellent.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Oloololo (Siria) Escarpment area on the western edge of the Mara — a scenic and less-crowded part of the reserve. Look for cheetahs, hyenas, and large elephant herds on the open plains. The escarpment offers breathtaking panoramic views of the entire Mara ecosystem.
day_by_day.afternoon: Birdwatching session along the Mara River and its tributaries. The Mara is home to over 450 bird species including the Martial Eagle, African Fish Eagle, Lilac-breasted Roller, and Secretarybird. A budget birding guide from the lodge can be arranged for KES 500–1,000.
day_by_day.evening: Relax at the lodge. Write travel notes or sketch wildlife you've observed. Optional: participate in a basic Swahili language lesson offered by lodge staff — a fun and free cultural experience.

meals.breakfast: Lodge breakfast: porridge, fresh fruit, toast with honey, and chai — KES 250–400
meals.lunch: Bush picnic or lodge canteen lunch: vegetable curry with rice and a soft drink — KES 350–500
meals.dinner: Lodge dinner: fish stew (tilapia), steamed vegetables, ugali, and fresh fruit dessert — KES 500–700

day_by_day.notes: July weather in the Mara averages 25°C with minimal rainfall (30mm for the month) — ideal for game viewing as vegetation is lower and animals concentrate near water sources. Mornings can be chilly (12–15°C), so pack a fleece or light jacket for early drives.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day game drive through the central Mara plains — the heart of the Great Migration. Spend the morning tracking large predator activity: lions on morning hunts, leopards resting in acacia trees, and wild dogs if you're lucky. Your guide will use radio contact with other drivers to locate key sightings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the full-day drive into the afternoon. Visit the Mara Triangle (managed by the Mara Conservancy) if accessible from your lodge — it tends to be less crowded and has excellent wildlife density. Pack a picnic lunch to maximize time in the field.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the lodge by sunset. Enjoy a longer rest evening — take a hot shower, hand-wash clothing, and recharge camera batteries. Dinner at the lodge with a review of the day's wildlife sightings.

meals.breakfast: Early lodge breakfast: scrambled eggs, sausage, toast, and fresh juice — KES 300–500
meals.lunch: Packed picnic lunch in the bush: sandwiches, boiled eggs, fruit, crisps, and water — KES 300–450
meals.dinner: Lodge dinner: beef stew with chapati, steamed greens, and a bowl of soup — KES 500–800

day_by_day.notes: A full-day game drive is the best value for your park entry fee — you pay once and stay all day. Carry at least 2 liters of water per person, sunscreen, and a hat. The shared game drive vehicle keeps costs low — confirm your slot with the lodge the evening before.

day_by_day.morning: Morning nature walk along the Mara River banks with an armed Maasai ranger. Observe hippo pods in the river, Nile crocodiles basking on the banks, and diverse birdlife in the riparian forest. Walking safaris offer a more intimate wildlife experience unavailable from a vehicle.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Talek area or a nearby community conservancy bordering the reserve. Community conservancies like Ol Kinyei or Naboisho offer budget-friendly game drives with fewer vehicles and a more exclusive experience. Proceeds support local Maasai communities.
day_by_day.evening: Attend an optional guided night game drive (if offered by your lodge or a local operator — approx. KES 1,500–2,500 per person). Spot nocturnal animals including aardvarks, porcupines, civets, and genets using a spotlight. Return for a late dinner.

meals.breakfast: Simple lodge breakfast: mandazi, chai, and sliced fruit — KES 200–300
meals.lunch: Local restaurant in Talek village: nyama choma with ugali and kachumbari — KES 400–600
meals.dinner: Lodge dinner: pasta with vegetable sauce, bread, and hot chocolate — KES 400–600

day_by_day.notes: The Talek gate area has a small cluster of local restaurants and shops where you can eat affordably and interact with local residents. Community conservancy fees are generally lower than the main reserve and the experience is equally rewarding. Always walk with a licensed ranger for safety.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicated cheetah and wild dog tracking morning drive on the open Mara plains. July is an excellent month to spot cheetahs as the short grass makes them more visible. Ask your guide to focus on the southeastern plains near the Sekenani area for the best chances.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rest and leisure afternoon at the lodge. Take advantage of the lodge's common areas to relax, read, or review your wildlife photographs. Optional: learn basic wildlife photography tips from a fellow traveler or guide — free and educational.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner walk to a scenic viewpoint near the lodge (guided). Watch the golden hour light transform the savanna. Return for a special budget-friendly braai (African BBQ) dinner at the lodge if available, or a standard communal dinner.

meals.breakfast: Lodge breakfast: French toast with honey, sliced papaya, and chai — KES 250–400
meals.lunch: Light lodge lunch: vegetable soup, bread rolls, and a cold drink — KES 250–400
meals.dinner: Braai/BBQ at the lodge: grilled meats, roasted corn, potato salad, and fresh juice — KES 600–900

day_by_day.notes: Mid-trip is a good time to review your budget and spending. Stock up on snacks (biscuits, nuts, dried fruit) from the Talek market to reduce meal costs during game drives. Check camera memory cards and batteries — you'll want maximum storage for the remaining days.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning drive to the Mara North Conservancy or Olare Motorogi Conservancy (if accessible and affordable via shared vehicle). These conservancies have exceptional leopard sightings and offer a premium wildlife experience at a fraction of luxury lodge prices when accessed on a budget shared drive.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the main reserve for an afternoon drive focusing on elephant herds near the Mara River. July often sees large elephant family groups moving through the area. Observe mother-calf interactions and the herds' social dynamics.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the lodge's local craft market or a nearby community market. Purchase affordable Maasai beadwork, soapstone carvings, or wooden figurines as souvenirs. Support local artisans by buying directly. Budget KES 500–2,000 for souvenirs.

meals.breakfast: Pre-dawn lodge snack: boiled eggs, bread, and thermos of chai — KES 150–250
meals.lunch: Packed bush lunch: rice and beans in a container, fruit, and water — KES 200–350
meals.dinner: Lodge dinner: chicken pilau (spiced rice), raita (yogurt dip), and vegetable salad — KES 500–700

day_by_day.notes: Bargaining is expected and acceptable at craft markets — start at 50% of the asking price and settle around 60–70%. Be respectful and friendly during negotiations. Avoid buying items made from wildlife products (shells, feathers, ivory) as these are illegal to export.

day_by_day.morning: Final full morning game drive — make it count! Request your guide to revisit your favorite spots or seek out any animals you haven't yet seen. Focus on the Big Five checklist and spend extra time observing lion prides with cubs if located. Capture final wildlife photographs and video.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the boutique stay and begin the journey back toward Nairobi via shared shuttle or matatu. Stop at Narok town for lunch and a brief exploration of the local market — a vibrant hub of Maasai culture and commerce. Browse fresh produce, spices, and local goods.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive in Nairobi in the early evening. Check into a budget guesthouse or hostel in the city (e.g., in the Westlands or Upper Hill areas — KES 1,500–3,000 per night). Enjoy a celebratory dinner at a local Nairobi restaurant to mark the end of your Mara adventure.

meals.breakfast: Final lodge breakfast: full spread of eggs, toast, fruit, and chai — KES 300–500
meals.lunch: Narok town restaurant: pilau rice with beef, kachumbari, and a cold Fanta — KES 350–500
meals.dinner: Nairobi local restaurant (e.g., Carnivore budget meals or a local nyama choma joint): mixed grill plate with ugali and greens — KES 600–1,000

day_by_day.notes: Confirm your return shuttle timing the night before. Narok is a good place to stock up on affordable Maasai crafts and fresh produce. Keep your valuables secure during the Nairobi arrival — use registered taxis or Uber/Bolt from the shuttle drop-off point to your guesthouse.

day_by_day.morning: Spend the final morning exploring Nairobi's wildlife and nature offerings. Visit Nairobi National Park (KES 1,000–1,500 entry for budget visitors) — the world's only national park within a capital city. Spot lions, rhinos, giraffes, and buffalos with the city skyline in the background. A remarkable final wildlife experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the David Sheldrick Wildlife Trust elephant orphanage (free or small donation) near Nairobi National Park — meet orphaned baby elephants being rehabilitated for release into the wild. Alternatively, visit the Giraffe Centre (KES 1,000 entry) to hand-feed endangered Rothschild giraffes.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Jomo Kenyatta International Airport for departure. Allow at least 3 hours before your flight for check-in, security, and immigration. Reflect on an incredible 10-day Kenyan adventure filled with unforgettable wildlife encounters, cultural experiences, and natural beauty.

meals.breakfast: Guesthouse breakfast: chai, mandazi, and a boiled egg — KES 150–300
meals.lunch: Nairobi National Park picnic or park canteen: packed sandwiches and fruit — KES 200–400
meals.dinner: Airport meal or pre-departure snack at a Nairobi café: samosas, chai, and a pastry — KES 300–500

day_by_day.notes: Nairobi traffic can be severe — allow extra travel time to the airport, especially during evening rush hour (4–7 PM). Use Uber or Bolt for reliable and metered transport (KES 800–1,500 to the airport from most city areas). Ensure all wildlife souvenirs comply with CITES regulations — no animal products. Keep your park receipts and travel documents organized for departure.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Nairobi Jomo Kenyatta International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Clear immigration, collect luggage, and meet your pre-arranged transfer driver.
day_by_day.afternoon: Scenic 5–6 hour road transfer from Nairobi to Maasai Mara National Reserve (approx. 270 km via the B3 highway through the Rift Valley escarpment). Enjoy stunning views of the Great Rift Valley en route. Arrive at your boutique stay in the Mara by early evening and complete check-in.
day_by_day.evening: Welcome orientation with your camp manager or guide — receive a briefing on safari safety, wildlife etiquette, and the week's itinerary. Enjoy a relaxed first evening at the lodge listening to the sounds of the African bush.

meals.breakfast: Grab a light snack or meal at Nairobi airport upon arrival (Java House or Artcaffe in the terminal — mid-range, KES 800–1,500)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or roadside stop at a local eatery along the B3 highway near Narok town — try nyama choma (roasted meat) with ugali (KES 600–1,000)
meals.dinner: Welcome dinner at your boutique lodge — typically a set three-course bush dinner featuring Kenyan staples like pilau rice, grilled chicken, and fresh vegetables (included or KES 2,500–4,000)

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book your Nairobi to Mara transfer in advance (shared shuttle ~KES 2,500 or private 4WD ~KES 8,000–12,000). The road can be bumpy after Narok — pack essentials in your day bag. July is peak Great Migration season so expect the reserve to be lively.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning game drive inside Maasai Mara National Reserve departing at 06:00. Focus on the Mara Triangle and Musiara Marsh areas — prime habitat for lion prides, cheetah, elephant, and buffalo. The golden morning light is perfect for wildlife photography.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to lodge for a late bush breakfast, then rest during the midday heat. Optional guided nature walk around the lodge perimeter with a Maasai ranger to learn about local flora, insects, and tracks (approx. 2 hours, KES 1,500–2,500 per person).
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner game drive along the Mara River at dusk — watch hippos and crocodiles at the river's edge as the sun sets over the savannah. Return to camp for dinner under the stars.

meals.breakfast: Full English-style bush breakfast served in the field or at the lodge — eggs, sausages, toast, fresh fruit, and Kenyan tea/coffee (included or KES 1,500–2,500)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the lodge — fresh salads, sandwiches, and grilled meats (KES 1,200–2,000)
meals.dinner: Three-course dinner at the lodge restaurant — roasted lamb, seasonal vegetables, and passion fruit cheesecake (included or KES 2,500–4,000)

day_by_day.notes: Wear neutral-colored clothing (khaki, olive, brown) for game drives. Bring a warm fleece — early morning temperatures can drop to 12–15°C. A quality pair of binoculars is highly recommended. July is optimal for Big Five sightings.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day Maasai Mara Great Migration Safari — depart at dawn (05:30) for the iconic wildebeest and zebra river crossings at the Mara River. Position near known crossing points with your guide. Witness millions of wildebeest, zebras, and gazelles braving crocodile-infested waters in one of nature's greatest spectacles.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Great Migration safari through the open plains of the Mara ecosystem. Track large wildebeest herds moving northward and observe predator activity — lions and cheetahs frequently hunt along migration routes. Enjoy a packed bush lunch in the field.
day_by_day.evening: Return to lodge by 18:30. Freshen up and join fellow guests for a communal campfire session with stories from your guide about the migration's ecological significance.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the lodge before departure — fresh fruit, yogurt, and coffee (included or KES 800–1,200)
meals.lunch: Packed bush picnic lunch prepared by the lodge — sandwiches, fruit, juice, and snacks enjoyed in the Mara plains (included with full-day safari or KES 1,000–1,500)
meals.dinner: Hearty dinner at the lodge — Kenyan beef stew with chapati, roasted sweet potatoes, and fresh mango sorbet (included or KES 2,500–3,500)

day_by_day.notes: The Great Migration river crossings are unpredictable — patience is key. Your guide will use radio communication with other guides to locate active crossings. This is the highlight experience of the trip; budget KES 8,000–15,000 for a dedicated full-day migration safari if not already included in your package.

day_by_day.morning: Maasai Cultural Village & Bush Dinner experience begins with a morning visit to an authentic Maasai boma (village) near the reserve. Meet the village elder, learn about traditional Maasai customs, observe the enkiama (jumping dance), and participate in fire-making and beadwork demonstrations.
day_by_day.afternoon: Guided walk through the surrounding bush with a Maasai warrior — learn about medicinal plants, animal tracking, and the Maasai's coexistence with wildlife. This half-day cultural immersion offers a unique perspective on life on the edge of the Mara.
day_by_day.evening: Bush Dinner Under the Stars — a magical setup in the open savannah with lanterns, a long table, and traditional Maasai songs performed around the fire. Feast on a specially prepared menu featuring nyama choma, githeri (maize and beans), sukuma wiki, and local honey dessert.

meals.breakfast: Lodge breakfast — fresh tropical fruits, scrambled eggs, and mandazi (Kenyan doughnuts) with chai tea (included or KES 1,200–2,000)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the Maasai village — traditional ugali with sour milk (fermented cow's milk) and vegetable stew, a genuine cultural experience (included in village visit fee or KES 500–800)
meals.dinner: Bush Dinner Under the Stars — multi-course traditional Kenyan feast in the open savannah (KES 4,500–7,000 per person or included in experience package)

day_by_day.notes: Bring small gifts for the Maasai village such as school supplies or sugar — check with your guide on appropriate gifts. The cultural village visit costs approximately KES 2,000–3,500 per person. Ask permission before photographing community members. The evening temperature drops — bring a warm layer for the bush dinner.

day_by_day.morning: Early departure from Maasai Mara at 06:00 for the drive north to Lake Nakuru National Park (approx. 3–4 hours via Narok and the B3). Check in to a mid-range lodge or tented camp near the park entrance upon arrival.
day_by_day.afternoon: Afternoon game drive inside Lake Nakuru National Park — a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Explore the lake shores and woodland areas searching for white and black rhinos, Rothschild's giraffes, lions, leopards, and the park's famous waterbuck herds.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset viewing at Baboon Cliff Lookout — a panoramic viewpoint offering sweeping views over the entire lake, its pink flamingo fringe, and the surrounding Rift Valley escarpment. Return to lodge for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at Mara lodge before departure — toast, eggs, and Kenyan coffee (included or KES 1,000–1,500)
meals.lunch: Lunch at a mid-range restaurant in Nakuru town upon arrival — try Gilani's Restaurant for Indian-Kenyan fusion cuisine (KES 1,000–1,800 per person)
meals.dinner: Dinner at your Lake Nakuru lodge — grilled tilapia fish (a local Rift Valley specialty), rice, and kachumbari (tomato-onion salad) (included or KES 2,000–3,500)

day_by_day.notes: Lake Nakuru park entry fees: KES 5,285 for non-residents (approximately USD 40). The flamingo population varies seasonally — July typically sees good numbers. Nakuru is also excellent for rhino sightings as it is a fenced sanctuary. Keep windows up near baboon troops.

day_by_day.morning: Lake Nakuru Flamingo & Bird Safari — full morning dedicated to birdwatching along the lake shores. Witness thousands to millions of lesser and greater flamingos creating a stunning pink carpet on the water's edge. Also spot pelicans, African fish eagles, and over 400 bird species recorded in the park.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to the southern end of the park to visit the Makalia Falls — a beautiful forested waterfall within the park. Short nature walk in the surrounding acacia woodland. Look out for leopards resting in the trees — Nakuru has a healthy leopard population.
day_by_day.evening: Return to lodge by 17:30. Optional visit to Nakuru town for a local craft market — purchase Maasai beadwork, soapstone carvings, and wooden crafts at the municipal market (budget KES 500–3,000 for souvenirs).

meals.breakfast: Lodge breakfast — fresh papaya, eggs to order, and whole-grain toast with local honey (included or KES 1,200–2,000)
meals.lunch: Packed picnic lunch by the lake shore — sandwiches, fresh fruit, and juice (arranged by lodge, KES 800–1,200)
meals.dinner: Dinner at lodge — slow-cooked goat curry with basmati rice, steamed greens, and fresh pineapple dessert (included or KES 2,000–3,500)

day_by_day.notes: Bring a telephoto lens for flamingo photography — the best shots are from the lake's edge in morning light. A good field guide to East African birds is a worthwhile investment. The park road to Makalia Falls can be muddy in rainy season — July is generally dry but carry wet weather gear.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning departure from Lake Nakuru heading east to Ol Pejeta Conservancy in Laikipia County (approx. 2.5–3 hour drive). Check in to your mid-range tented camp or lodge within or near the conservancy.
day_by_day.afternoon: Ol Pejeta Conservancy Rhino Tracking — join an expert ranger on a guided foot safari to track both black and white rhinos. Ol Pejeta is home to the last two northern white rhinos on Earth (Najin and Fatu) — a deeply moving conservation experience. Learn about anti-poaching efforts and rhino conservation programs.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the Sweetwaters Chimpanzee Sanctuary within Ol Pejeta — the only place in Kenya where you can see chimpanzees. Evening feeding time offers excellent close-up viewing. Return to camp for a conservation-themed dinner talk with a ranger.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at Nakuru lodge before departure (included or KES 1,000–1,500)
meals.lunch: Lunch at Ol Pejeta's Morani Restaurant inside the conservancy — grilled meats, salads, and fresh juices in a relaxed bush setting (KES 1,500–2,500)
meals.dinner: Dinner at your tented camp — wood-fired pizza or pasta with a Kenyan twist, served under a canopy of stars (included or KES 2,500–4,000)

day_by_day.notes: Ol Pejeta conservancy entry: approximately KES 5,000 per person per day for non-residents. The northern white rhino viewing requires an additional small fee and advance booking. Rhino tracking on foot is one of Africa's most exclusive wildlife experiences — book this activity in advance. Photography of the northern white rhinos is permitted and encouraged to raise awareness.

day_by_day.morning: Full morning game drive inside Ol Pejeta Conservancy — one of East Africa's premier wildlife destinations with lions, leopards, cheetahs, elephants, buffalo, and over 100 other mammal species. The conservancy's open grasslands and riverine forest offer diverse habitats and excellent game viewing.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive south from Ol Pejeta toward Amboseli National Park (approx. 4–5 hours via Nairobi Southern Bypass). Arrive at your Amboseli lodge in the late afternoon and check in with views of Mount Kilimanjaro on the horizon.
day_by_day.evening: First sunset in Amboseli — sit on the lodge terrace with a sundowner drink watching Kilimanjaro's snow-capped peak glow pink and gold at dusk. This is one of Africa's most iconic views and a perfect way to end the driving day.

meals.breakfast: Full bush breakfast at Ol Pejeta camp — eggs, bacon, fresh fruit, and strong Kenyan coffee (included or KES 1,500–2,500)
meals.lunch: Roadside lunch stop en route — try a local restaurant in Naivasha or Nairobi outskirts serving nyama choma and pilau rice (KES 800–1,500)
meals.dinner: Welcome dinner at Amboseli lodge — roasted chicken with Kenyan spiced rice, steamed vegetables, and passion fruit tart (included or KES 2,500–4,000)

day_by_day.notes: The drive from Ol Pejeta to Amboseli is long — consider a comfort stop in Nairobi. Alternatively, a domestic flight from Nanyuki (near Ol Pejeta) to Amboseli (approx. USD 150–250 one way) saves 4–5 hours and offers spectacular aerial views of the Rift Valley. July is dry season in Amboseli — roads are in good condition.

day_by_day.morning: Amboseli Elephant Watching with Kilimanjaro Backdrop — depart at 06:00 for a dedicated elephant safari in the swamp and open plains of Amboseli National Park. Amboseli hosts one of Africa's largest free-roaming elephant herds (over 1,600 individuals). Watch massive bull elephants, family groups with calves, and matriarchs moving against the iconic backdrop of Mount Kilimanjaro.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Amboseli Elephant Research Project observation point — the longest-running elephant research project in the world (est. 1972). Learn about individual elephant identification, family dynamics, and conservation challenges. Continue afternoon game drive through the Enkongo Narok swamp — home to hippos, buffalo, and hundreds of waterbirds.
day_by_day.evening: Maasai cultural sundowner — a local Maasai guide leads a short walk to a scenic viewpoint for sunset drinks accompanied by traditional songs. The combination of Kilimanjaro at dusk and Maasai culture creates an unforgettable final evening in the bush.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at lodge before game drive — fruit, yogurt, and coffee (included or KES 800–1,200)
meals.lunch: Midday return to lodge for a full lunch — buffet spread featuring Kenyan and international dishes, fresh salads, and cold drinks (included or KES 1,800–2,800)
meals.dinner: Special farewell bush dinner at Amboseli — slow-roasted lamb, roasted root vegetables, and a traditional Kenyan dessert of mandazi with honey (included or KES 3,000–5,000)

day_by_day.notes: Amboseli park entry: approximately KES 5,285 per person per day for non-residents. Morning light is best for Kilimanjaro views — the mountain often clouds over by mid-morning. Bring a wide-angle lens for landscape shots and a telephoto for elephant close-ups. Dust can be heavy in the dry season — protect camera equipment.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise game drive in Amboseli — one last opportunity to photograph elephants with Kilimanjaro at golden hour. Return to lodge by 09:00 for a full breakfast and to pack and check out.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer from Amboseli to Nairobi Jomo Kenyatta International Airport (approx. 4 hours via the C103 road through Emali). En route, stop at a Maasai craft cooperative near Kajiado for last-minute souvenir shopping — quality beadwork, fabrics, and carvings at fair-trade prices (KES 500–5,000).
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Nairobi airport with time to spare for check-in and departure formalities. Enjoy a final Kenyan meal at the airport — Java House serves excellent Kenyan coffee and light meals. Depart Kenya with extraordinary memories of the Mara migration, Kilimanjaro elephants, northern white rhinos, and the warmth of Maasai culture.

meals.breakfast: Full lodge breakfast before check-out — fresh tropical fruits, eggs, toast, and a final cup of Kenyan AA coffee (included or KES 1,500–2,500)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch box from the lodge for the road journey — or stop at a roadside café in Emali town (KES 600–1,000)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Nairobi airport — Java House or Artcaffe for a relaxed final Kenyan meal: chicken wrap, fresh juice, and a slice of carrot cake (KES 1,500–2,500)

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours at Nairobi airport before international departure for check-in, security, and immigration. Kenyan wildlife products (ivory, skins, feathers) are strictly prohibited for export under CITES regulations — only purchase certified crafts. Keep USD cash for any last-minute park fees or tips. Standard tipping: game drivers KES 500–1,000 per day; lodge staff KES 200–500 per day.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Kenya Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Maasai Mara National Reserve, Narok County Boutique Stay
hotel.location: Maasai Mara National Reserve, Narok County

experiences.name: Maasai Mara Great Migration Safari
experiences.description: Witness the world-famous Great Migration where millions of wildebeest, zebras, and gazelles cross the Mara River in a dramatic spectacle. Game drives in open 4x4 vehicles offer close encounters with the Big Five including lions, elephants, leopards, buffaloes, and rhinos in their natural habitat.
experiences.location: Maasai Mara National Reserve, Narok County

experiences.name: Amboseli Elephant Watching with Kilimanjaro Backdrop
experiences.description: Observe the largest free-roaming elephant herds in Africa against the stunning backdrop of Mount Kilimanjaro. Amboseli is renowned for its large elephant population and offers exceptional photography opportunities with dramatic landscapes including swamps, savannah, and volcanic ash plains.

experiences.name: Ol Pejeta Conservancy Rhino Tracking
experiences.description: Track both black and white rhinos on foot with expert rangers at Ol Pejeta, home to the last two northern white rhinos on Earth. The conservancy also shelters chimpanzees, lions, and wild dogs. A guided bush walk brings you intimately close to nature in a way traditional game drives cannot.

experiences.name: Lake Nakuru Flamingo & Bird Safari
experiences.description: Explore Lake Nakuru National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site famous for its millions of pink flamingos that paint the lake's shores in vivid color. The park also hosts Rothschild giraffes, white rhinos, and over 450 bird species, making it a paradise for nature lovers and birdwatchers.
experiences.location: Lake Nakuru National Park, Nakuru County

experiences.name: Maasai Cultural Village & Bush Dinner Under the Stars
experiences.description: Immerse yourself in authentic Maasai culture with a guided village visit, traditional dances, and storytelling around a campfire. Cap the evening with a bush dinner under a canopy of stars in the open savannah, enjoying locally inspired cuisine including nyama choma (roasted meat) and ugali while listening to the sounds of the African wilderness.
experiences.location: Maasai Mara Conservancy Villages, Narok County

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Nairobi Jomo Kenyatta International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Upon landing, you will be met by a dedicated luxury concierge and transferred via private charter flight or premium 4x4 vehicle to your boutique stay in the Maasai Mara National Reserve.
day_by_day.afternoon: Scenic transfer to the Maasai Mara (approximately 1.5-hour charter flight or 5-hour luxury road transfer). Settle into your boutique camp, enjoy a welcome drink and orientation with your personal ranger. Take a short introductory sunset game drive around the reserve perimeter to acclimatize and spot resident wildlife including lion, elephant, and giraffe.
day_by_day.evening: Welcome bush dinner under the stars at your boutique camp, set around a private fire pit. Toast your arrival with sundowners and enjoy a curated three-course dinner prepared by the camp's private chef, featuring locally inspired Kenyan cuisine with international touches.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable — in-flight or airport lounge dining prior to arrival
meals.lunch: Light welcome spread at the camp upon arrival: fresh tropical fruits, artisan sandwiches, and cold-pressed juices
meals.dinner: Private welcome bush dinner at camp: roasted lamb chops with Maasai spiced rub, grilled seasonal vegetables, and a decadent chocolate fondant dessert paired with premium South African wines

day_by_day.notes: Pack light for the charter flight as luggage is limited to soft bags of 15 kg. Confirm charter flight details with your concierge 48 hours in advance. Sunset game drive begins at approximately 16:30 and returns before dark.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning full-day Maasai Mara Great Migration Safari — depart at 06:00 in a private open-roof 4x4 Land Cruiser with your expert guide. Witness the iconic spectacle of millions of wildebeest, zebras, and Thomson's gazelles in their natural habitat. Focus on the Mara River crossing points where dramatic predator-prey interactions frequently occur during July.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Great Migration Safari through the afternoon, tracking herds across the golden savannah. Enjoy a gourmet bush picnic lunch served in the field by your camp team, complete with chilled wines and linen-set table settings in the wilderness. Look out for the Big Five — lion, leopard, elephant, buffalo, and rhino — as well as cheetah and hyena.
day_by_day.evening: Return to camp by 18:30 for hot outdoor showers and relaxation. Enjoy pre-dinner cocktails at the camp's elevated viewing deck overlooking the plains. Dinner is a candlelit four-course affair at the main dining tent, with storytelling from your head ranger about the day's wildlife encounters.

meals.breakfast: Full English breakfast at camp before departure: eggs cooked to order, smoked bacon, grilled tomatoes, fresh pastries, Kenyan AA coffee and fresh fruit juices
meals.lunch: Luxury bush picnic in the Mara: charcuterie boards, fresh baguettes, smoked salmon, gourmet wraps, seasonal salads, and chilled Sauvignon Blanc
meals.dinner: Four-course candlelit dinner at camp: cream of butternut soup, pan-seared Nile perch with lemon caper butter, braised beef short rib with mashed sweet potato, and passion fruit panna cotta

day_by_day.notes: July is peak Great Migration season — river crossings are most likely at Mara River between 07:00 and 10:00. Bring binoculars, a zoom lens camera, and warm layers for the early morning drive as temperatures can dip to 12°C at dawn.

day_by_day.morning: Exclusive hot air balloon safari over the Maasai Mara at sunrise — depart camp at 05:30 for a pre-dawn transfer to the launch site. Float silently above the golden savannah for approximately 60–75 minutes, witnessing the Great Migration herds, river systems, and predators from a breathtaking aerial perspective with your certified pilot.
day_by_day.afternoon: Post-balloon champagne breakfast in the bush — a white-linen celebration breakfast served in the open wilderness upon landing, a classic Mara tradition. Return to camp by midday for leisure time: enjoy a spa treatment at the camp's bush spa (massage, aromatherapy, or hot stone therapy), relax by the plunge pool, or take a guided nature walk on the camp's private conservancy land.
day_by_day.evening: Maasai Cultural Village Visit & Bush Dinner Under the Stars — be escorted by your ranger to a neighboring authentic Maasai village at dusk. Participate in traditional dances, learn about Maasai warrior culture, and tour the boma (homestead). Return for an extraordinary private bush dinner under a canopy of stars, with traditional Maasai songs performed by village elders around the fire.

meals.breakfast: Champagne bush breakfast in the Mara after the balloon landing: smoked salmon blinis, scrambled eggs, fresh croissants, tropical fruit platters, and Moët & Chandon Champagne
meals.lunch: Light poolside lunch at camp: grilled tilapia tacos, avocado and mango salad, fresh lemonade, and coconut ice cream
meals.dinner: Exclusive bush dinner under the stars: Maasai-inspired nyama choma (roasted meat), ugali with sukuma wiki, honey-glazed chicken, and traditional Kenyan chai to close

day_by_day.notes: Hot air balloon safaris must be booked and paid in advance — typically USD 450–600 per person. Weather permitting; your concierge will confirm the evening before. Wear closed shoes for the Maasai village visit out of respect for local customs.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided walking safari within the Maasai Mara conservancy — depart at 06:30 with an armed ranger and expert naturalist for an intimate on-foot exploration of the bush. Learn to track wildlife by footprints, study medicinal plants, and observe smaller creatures often missed on vehicle safaris. This immersive experience brings you closer to the ecosystem at a human pace.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to camp for lunch and a midday rest. In the afternoon, embark on a private photography-focused game drive with a specialist wildlife photography guide. The soft afternoon light (15:00–18:00) is ideal for capturing dramatic portraits of predators, migration herds, and the sweeping Mara landscape. Your guide will position the vehicle for optimal angles and lighting.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner cocktails on a scenic hilltop overlooking the Mara plains — your ranger will set up a private drinks station at a panoramic viewpoint for a magical golden hour experience. Return to camp for a relaxed dinner at the main dining area, with a special focus on Kenyan coastal Swahili cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Continental breakfast at camp before the walk: fresh fruit, granola with Kenyan honey, yogurt parfaits, whole grain toast, and Kenyan single-origin coffee
meals.lunch: Three-course lunch at camp: chilled gazpacho, grilled chicken with roasted root vegetables, and a light lemon tart
meals.dinner: Swahili-inspired dinner at camp: coconut prawn curry with basmati rice, pilau spiced lamb, kachumbari salad, and mandazi (Kenyan doughnuts) with tamarind dipping sauce

day_by_day.notes: Walking safaris require a minimum fitness level and closed sturdy shoes. Children under 12 are generally not permitted on walking safaris. The photography game drive is best with a 200–600mm telephoto lens — equipment rental can be arranged through the camp.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Maasai Mara by private charter flight to Amboseli National Park (approximately 45-minute flight). Check in to your luxury tented camp at the foot of Mount Kilimanjaro. After settling in, begin the Amboseli Elephant Watching Safari — join your private guide to locate and observe the largest free-roaming elephant herds in Africa, many of which are part of long-studied family groups with known histories.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Amboseli elephant experience through the afternoon with a dedicated full-day safari in the park. Mount Kilimanjaro (5,895 m) serves as a stunning snow-capped backdrop for photography. Explore the park's swamps, acacia woodlands, and open plains, also spotting lion, cheetah, buffalo, and over 400 bird species including superb starlings and crowned cranes.
day_by_day.evening: Return to camp for sundowners on your private tent veranda with unobstructed Kilimanjaro views. Enjoy a sophisticated dinner at the camp's open-air restaurant, with al fresco dining under the African sky and the silhouette of Kilimanjaro glowing in the moonlight.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at Mara camp before departure: eggs Benedict, smoked meats, fresh juices, and Kenyan tea
meals.lunch: Bush lunch in Amboseli served in the field: artisan sandwiches, cold meats, fresh salads, and sparkling water with citrus
meals.dinner: Al fresco dinner at Amboseli camp: wild mushroom risotto starter, slow-roasted game meat with truffle jus, Kilimanjaro vegetable medley, and dark chocolate mousse with berry compote

day_by_day.notes: Amboseli's elephant herds are best observed near the Enkongo Narok swamp in the morning when they come to drink and bathe. Kilimanjaro is most visible in the early morning before clouds gather — your guide will position you optimally for photography at sunrise.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise game drive in Amboseli beginning at 06:00 — the golden morning light against Kilimanjaro creates some of the most iconic wildlife photography conditions in Africa. Focus on elephant family dynamics, observing matriarchs leading their herds to water. Your naturalist guide will share in-depth knowledge about individual elephants tracked by the Amboseli Elephant Research Project.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Amboseli Maasai community on the park's border for a cultural interaction — learn about the traditional coexistence between Maasai pastoralists and wildlife. Participate in a beadwork workshop and purchase authentic handcrafted jewelry directly from artisans. Return to camp for a leisurely afternoon with spa treatments, pool time, or guided birdwatching around the camp's waterhole.
day_by_day.evening: Private dinner experience in a specially prepared location within the conservancy — your camp team sets up an intimate table for two (or your group) with lanterns, candles, and fine linens amid the wilderness. A private chef prepares a bespoke five-course tasting menu while a Maasai musician performs traditional songs.

meals.breakfast: Sunrise breakfast basket delivered to your tent veranda: fresh pastries, fruit, yogurt, boiled eggs, and a thermos of Kenyan coffee to enjoy with Kilimanjaro views
meals.lunch: Elegant camp lunch: grilled Nile perch with mango salsa, quinoa salad with roasted vegetables, and fresh tropical fruit sorbet
meals.dinner: Five-course private wilderness dinner: amuse-bouche of smoked papaya, wild herb soup, pan-seared duck breast, cheese board with Kenyan honey, and a decadent caramel tart with vanilla cream

day_by_day.notes: The private dinner experience should be requested and confirmed with camp management at least 24 hours in advance. Evening temperatures in Amboseli can drop to 14°C — bring a light jacket or shawl. Sundowners near the swamp at 17:30 offer spectacular elephant silhouette photography opportunities.

day_by_day.morning: Private charter flight from Amboseli to Ol Pejeta Conservancy in Laikipia (approximately 1-hour flight). Check in to your luxury lodge within or adjacent to the conservancy. Begin the Ol Pejeta Rhino Tracking Experience — join expert rangers and trackers on foot to locate and observe both black and white rhinos, including the last two northern white rhinos on Earth, Najin and Fatu, in their specially protected enclosure.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Ol Pejeta on a private game drive — the conservancy is home to the Big Five and boasts the highest density of black rhinos in East Africa. Visit the Sweetwaters Chimpanzee Sanctuary, a unique feature of Ol Pejeta that provides a haven for rescued chimpanzees from across Africa. Enjoy a guided tour of the sanctuary with primatologist commentary.
day_by_day.evening: Return to your luxury lodge for a relaxed evening. Enjoy cocktails at the lodge's bar overlooking the conservancy's waterhole, where nocturnal wildlife often appears after dark. Dinner is served at the lodge's fine dining restaurant with panoramic views of the Aberdare Mountains.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at Amboseli camp before departure: French toast with berry compote, smoked salmon, eggs to order, and fresh pressed juices
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic lunch at Ol Pejeta: artisan bread, aged cheeses, cured meats, fresh fruit, and chilled rosé wine served in a scenic conservancy location
meals.dinner: Lodge fine dining: roasted beet and goat cheese salad, pan-seared springbok loin with red wine reduction, roasted garlic mashed potatoes, and a warm lava cake with Kenyan coffee ice cream

day_by_day.notes: Rhino tracking on foot requires a moderate fitness level. The northern white rhino enclosure visit is a deeply moving conservation experience — your guide will brief you on the ongoing IVF conservation program to save the subspecies from extinction. Photography is permitted but flash is prohibited near the rhinos.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning guided horseback safari at Ol Pejeta (06:00 departure) — ride through the open conservancy on well-trained horses alongside zebras, giraffes, and eland in one of Africa's most unique wildlife experiences. This perspective at animal eye-level creates extraordinary encounters impossible from a vehicle. Suitable for both beginners and experienced riders.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private charter flight from Ol Pejeta to Lake Nakuru (approximately 30-minute flight or 1.5-hour luxury road transfer). Arrive at your premium lodge on the shores of Lake Nakuru National Park. Begin the Lake Nakuru Flamingo & Bird Safari — explore this UNESCO World Heritage Site renowned for its vast flocks of pink flamingos, pelicans, and over 450 bird species in a spectacular Rift Valley setting.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner cruise on Lake Nakuru (if available through your lodge) or a scenic hilltop viewpoint overlooking the lake's pink shores at golden hour. Return to your lodge for dinner, featuring a focus on fresh Rift Valley produce and lake fish. Enjoy a stargazing session with a resident astronomer on the lodge's open viewing deck.

meals.breakfast: Pre-ride light breakfast at lodge: energy bars, fresh fruit, yogurt, and strong Kenyan coffee served at 05:30
meals.lunch: Post-flight welcome lunch at Lake Nakuru lodge: grilled tilapia from the Rift Valley lakes, fresh garden salad, and homemade sourdough bread
meals.dinner: Rift Valley dinner experience: cream of avocado soup, pan-fried Lake Nakuru tilapia with lemon herb butter, roasted Rift Valley vegetables, and a classic Kenyan mandazi dessert platter

day_by_day.notes: Horseback safari requires advance booking and a rider assessment — inform your concierge of any riding experience beforehand. Lake Nakuru's flamingo population fluctuates based on algae levels; July typically sees large concentrations. The park is also excellent for white and black rhino sightings along the lake's forested edges.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day Lake Nakuru immersive safari experience — depart at 06:00 for a comprehensive exploration of the national park. Beyond the flamingos, track Rothschild's giraffes (one of the most endangered giraffe subspecies), white rhinos grazing on the lake's edge, and large troops of baboons and colobus monkeys in the yellow fever acacia forests. Climb to Baboon Cliff viewpoint for a panoramic aerial view of the entire lake.
day_by_day.afternoon: Guided birdwatching walk along the lake shore with an ornithologist guide — Lake Nakuru is considered one of the greatest ornithological spectacles on Earth. Identify pelicans, cormorants, African fish eagles, and the iconic pink carpet of flamingos up close. Return to lodge for a midday spa session: choose from a signature Kenyan coffee body scrub, hot stone massage, or aromatherapy treatment.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell gala dinner at the lodge — a celebratory multi-course dinner marking the penultimate evening of your Kenya journey. The lodge sets up a special private dining experience with premium wine pairings, live acoustic Kenyan music, and a personalized menu reflecting the culinary highlights of your entire trip.

meals.breakfast: Full lodge breakfast: eggs any style, fresh pastries, tropical fruit buffet, smoked fish, Kenyan chai, and freshly squeezed juices
meals.lunch: Elegant lodge lunch: Caesar salad with grilled chicken, mushroom and truffle pasta, and a refreshing watermelon granita
meals.dinner: Farewell gala dinner with wine pairing: oysters with mignonette, lobster bisque, prime beef tenderloin with Bordelaise sauce, artisan cheese board, and a signature Kenyan chocolate and coffee tasting dessert paired with a premium Kenyan single-origin espresso

day_by_day.notes: Request your preferred spa treatment at least 24 hours in advance to ensure therapist availability. The farewell dinner wine pairing should be pre-arranged with the lodge sommelier — inform them of any dietary restrictions or wine preferences when booking.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise game drive in Lake Nakuru National Park — a last golden-hour opportunity to photograph the flamingo-lined lake shores and resident wildlife. Capture the magic of the Rift Valley at dawn before returning to the lodge for a leisurely final breakfast. Take time to collect any last-minute souvenirs from the lodge's curated boutique, featuring authentic Kenyan art, jewelry, and conservation-supporting crafts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer from Lake Nakuru to Nairobi (approximately 2-hour scenic road journey through the Rift Valley escarpment, or 30-minute charter flight). Upon arrival in Nairobi, enjoy a premium farewell experience at one of Nairobi's finest restaurants or the Karen Blixen Museum area for a cultural send-off. If time permits before your departure flight, visit the Giraffe Centre or David Sheldrick Wildlife Trust for a final wildlife encounter.
day_by_day.evening: VIP transfer to Jomo Kenyatta International Airport with private lounge access. Your concierge will assist with all check-in formalities and luggage handling. Depart Kenya with extraordinary memories of one of the world's greatest wildlife destinations.

meals.breakfast: Grand final breakfast at Lake Nakuru lodge: full buffet spread with made-to-order eggs, smoked salmon, fresh pastries, tropical fruits, and a farewell Kenyan coffee ceremony
meals.lunch: Farewell lunch at a premium Nairobi restaurant (e.g., Talisman Restaurant in Karen or Carnivore Restaurant): signature Kenyan dishes, fresh juices, and a celebratory dessert
meals.dinner: Premium airport lounge dining or in-flight dining on your departure flight

day_by_day.notes: Confirm your departure flight time with your concierge and plan the Nairobi transfer accordingly, allowing at least 3 hours before international departure. Export restrictions apply to wildlife products — ensure all souvenirs purchased are certified and legally compliant. Your concierge can assist with documentation for any items purchased during the trip.
